chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: Atlantic City and the German restaurant job
summary: The Fowler band played Atlantic City and a classy German restaurant on 59th Street, with repertoire of classics and light music at good pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Now, we were rehearsing the group, Monte Carlo, we were playing, "Time Goes," "Passez Doubles" (PHONETIC). We had that type of band. And it was beautiful. Then we got a job to go to Atlantic City. (Inaudible) one of the clubs at Atlantic City. But it seems as though Charlie Johnson would usually go down there in the summer but we got the job. And oh, we had a beautiful time, man. I really got it together. And I turned 19, I got my mustache and I was really something special, then. Oh, yes, indeed. And I'd make the scene, have a certain amount saved up (inaudible).

But we were to go into a place on 59th (inaudible). It was a German place, it was a big restaurant, one of the high class restaurants, and we had to play in the afternoon. You had to play in the afternoon, we had to play the classics and airs and everything. Then at night we'd play for a lot of people, not too loud, (inaudible). But it was a beautiful job and the salary
How much were they paying at that time?
